blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Whonnock

items.t: Form B diligence (the frame, if a strata townhouse ever trades here): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. No Whonnock complex exists in for this to attach to today; the frame is stated so a future listing is diligenced correctly rather than assumed fee-simple.

: the stock that does exist here is fee-simple acreage housing, which carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees; municipal rules (Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019), ALR rules where they apply, and any registered covenants govern instead. A buyer importing strata expectations onto a Whonnock acreage — or strata fees onto a hypothetical fee-simple townhouse — is applying the wrong frame in both directions.

Suites, SSMUH and ALR: one secondary suite per lot in listed zones including A-1, A-2 and A-3, contained within the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not within the floodplain area; eligible single-detached and duplex lots may have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws. On ALR parcels the provincial ALR Use Regulation also governs: one secondary suite in the principal residence (s. 31) and an additional residence only if the s. 32 conditions are met. ALR status is per-parcel on ALC mapping; wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database; onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation (setbacks including 30 m from a well unless professional advice is obtained).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Whonnock

items.t: Zoning and OCP: The Albion Area Plan (adopted October 28, 2025) does not cover Whonnock.

Lougheed Transit Corridor — adopted position, with the correction stated: cite the corridor as adopted January 27, 2026 per the City record — OCP Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021 received third reading and adoption on January 27, 2026, the City issued a news release on February 4, 2026, and the corridor ends at 221 Street, far west of Whonnock, so it does not designate Whonnock parcels.

Suites and added units, as the City and the ALR Regulation state them: one secondary suite per lot is permitted in listed zones including A-1, A-2 and A-3, contained within the single detached building, to a maximum of 40% of gross floor area, and not in the Floodplain Area. On ALR parcels the provincial ALR Use Regulation also governs: it permits one secondary suite in the principal residence (s.31) and an additional residence only if the s.32 conditions are met.

ALR rules for Whonnock's agricultural land: subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s.6; Strata Property Act, s.239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s.21(1)). Residence caps: one principal residence per parcel, maximum 500 m²; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; one additional residence capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. Farm class (BC Assessment) has three tiers: $2,500 of gross farm income at 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha, with applications by October 31. A flat "$2,500+" figure is not correct.

Property transfer tax — worked anchors for acreage pricing: 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2,000,000, 3% above $2,000,000, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3,000,000. First-time buyers' and newly built home exemptions are HOME exemptions — a bare lot's eligibility is not confirmed here.

items.t: Main roads and transit: Lougheed Highway (Hwy 7) and Dewdney Trunk Road are the east–west roads; 272 Street and 280 Street run north–south, with 112 Avenue east–west. TransLink route 701 (Coquitlam Central Station / Haney Place / Maple Ridge East / Mission City Station) runs east on Dewdney Trunk Road — most east trips end at Dewdney Trunk Road at 248 Street, and some weekday trips continue non-stop from Haney Place to Mission City Station. There is no West Coast Express station in this sub-area; the nearest stations are outside the sub-area (Port Haney / Maple Ridge to the west, Mission City to the east).

Recreation and hospital: Whonnock Lake Park as above; no City recreation centre or library branch inside this sub-area was verified — the Maple Ridge Leisure Centre, 11925 Haney Place, and the Maple Ridge Public Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library), 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, are in Town Centre to the west. Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, is the community hospital for Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows with 24/7 emergency care; the Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 121 – 11900 Haney Place.

Whonnock: streets and boundaries

items.t: Whonnock is Maple Ridge's rural east edge, and the City publishes no boundary for the neighbourhood or the board sub-area.
Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) and Dewdney Trunk Road are the east-west roads, with 272 Street, 280 Street and 112 Avenue as the local grid.
The City lists Selvey Park, Whonnock Lake Park and Whonnock Lake Centre as the Whonnock facilities on its neighbourhood page.

blocks.text: Whonnock: the housing stock

items.t: The stock is freehold detached houses on acreages, not strata housing, with barns, workshops and horse facilities on the larger parcels.
Zone minimum lot areas under Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 run from RS-2 at 0.4 hectares and RS-3 at 0.8 or 2.0 hectares to A-1 at 2.0 hectares, A-2 at 4.0 hectares and A-3 at 8.0 hectares.

blocks.text: Whonnock: rules that affect buyers

items.t: One secondary suite per lot is permitted in zones including A-1, A-2 and A-3, inside the detached house, to 40% of gross floor area, and not in the floodplain area.
No Whonnock area plan exists; the Official Community Plan (OCP) and its rural designations govern, updated November 25, 2025.

blocks.text: Whonnock: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Whonnock Lake Park has a small sandy beach, swimming area, hiking trails and a playground, with the Ridge Canoe and Kayak Club based on Whonnock Lake.
Whonnock Lake Centre is at 27871 113 Avenue, the local hall for an area with no recreation centre or library branch of its own.
The nearest library and leisure centre are in the Town Centre to the west: Maple Ridge Public Library at 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road and the Leisure Centre at 11925 Haney Place.
Route 701's east trips mostly end at Dewdney Trunk Road at 248 Street, west of Whonnock, so route 749 is the in-area bus.
A property described as Ruskin in its own text can still sit in the Whonnock board sub-area at the east edge, so search both names.
Heritage buildings stand on River Road, 272 Street and the Lougheed Highway frontage; a heritage check belongs in diligence for older houses on those roads.

blocks.text: Whonnock: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check ALR status for the exact parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder before valuing any future use.
Check the well record in GWELLS and the septic filing against the Sewerage System Regulation's 30-metre well setback on every acreage purchase.
Check City floodplain mapping for low land near the Fraser River and Whonnock Creek, because suites are prohibited in the floodplain area.
Neither the ALR map nor the floodplain map states well yield or septic condition; both need property-level records and inspection.
